drafted_from: tool:find-high-pitched-stretches-of-a-recording's row in tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/tool-rows.json, its script in tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/do-work/ and the tests in tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/test/
start_here: Say to your AI: "Find the stretches of recordings/vid-a.wav spoken between 200 and 600 Hz and write them to the pitch folder." It runs tool:find-high-pitched-stretches-of-a-recording on your computer.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it reads one settings row of yours (record:setting:measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging~<scope_kind>~<scope_id>) or the settings you pass, and works on files in the show's folder.
instructions: 1. Clone the repository https://github.com/Trillion-X/trillion-workshop and check the needs listed on the row (python 3 and its libraries, ffmpeg where named).

2. Your AI reads the row with run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools, method tools:list and input {"tool":"tool:find-high-pitched-stretches-of-a-recording"}, saves your settings row (records:read record:setting:measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging~<scope_kind>~<scope_id>) to a file and puts it in the request as settings_record, or passes settings.

3. It runs: python3 -I trillion-workshop/tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/do-work/find_voice_by_pitch.py < REQUEST.json. REQUEST.json holds audio (one recording), out_dir and your band as settings or settings_record.

4. Run show/show_runs.py <out_dir>/<id>.json <captions.json3> to see each run with its caption words, then say which runs are the character; pitch alone also catches every other high voice, so use tool:find-when-a-character-speaks to tell them apart.

worked_examples.title: Two high-pitched runs in one recording
worked_examples.ask: Find the high-pitched stretches in vid-a.
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/do-work/find_voice_by_pitch.py (no test runs it: it needs librosa and ffmpeg). The AI reads the row with tools:list, then runs python3 -I trillion-workshop/tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/do-work/find_voice_by_pitch.py < REQUEST.json with REQUEST.json = {"audio": "recordings/vid-a.wav", "out_dir": "pitch", "settings": {"pitch_run_band_low_hz": 200.0, "pitch_run_band_high_hz": 600.0}}; the recording's voiced pitch holds two runs of at least 0.5 s in 200-600 Hz, 8.5-10.0 s and 30.0-35.0 s.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result": {"id": "vid-a", "json": "pitch/vid-a.json", "hi_s": 6.5, "runs": 2}}; pitch/vid-a.json lists the two runs (start, end, f0_median, hi_share) and pitch/vid-a.f0.npy holds the pitch of each voiced frame.
